thread:
maria: Quick heads-up before I hand off — doing a quick sweep of alert routing for tonight's quiet window. TL;DR: I adjusted a couple of noisy alerts and added a fallback route for batch GPU jobs. Please ack if you see anything risky.

jake: Which alerts did you touch?

maria: CPU-High on the batch-gpu pool was spamming during nightly jobs so I raised the threshold (80% -> 92%) and extended the window to 5m for that route only. Also added a mute rule for the repeated `kv-cache-warmup` alerts between 00:00-05:00 PST. No changes to model-serving latency SLOs.

maria: Example mute rule I applied:
```
mute_rules:
  - name: kv-cache-warmup
    channel: #eng-oncall
    hours: 00:00-05:00
    scope: batch-pool
```

oncall-bot: Reminder: Oncall shift swap scheduled — @sophia becomes primary at 23:00 PST.

sophia: ack — I'll take primary. Did we change any latency or error escalation paths?

maria: No latency SLO edits. Only routing fallback changed: if `model-serving.latency.p95` fires and the primary fails to acknowledge for 3m, it falls back to `dedicated-escalation` which pages oncall.

tim: Can you paste the fallback policy snippet so I can update my runbook?

maria: Sure — added a lightweight policy entry: 
```
fallback_policies:
  - from: model-serving*
    if_unacked: 180s
    fallback_to: dedicated-escalation
    dedup_on: instance_id
```

ben: FYI I'll be doing a short deploy of the checkpoint pruning job at 00:30. It might briefly spike GPU memory and trigger some alerts — I'll include the `[deploy:checkpoint-prune]` tag in the deploy message so filters ignore it.

maria: Perfect — that tag will be part of the mute filter. Also please add the `safety:quiet-window` flag so we don't escalate during the planned window.

sophia: I'll be primary but I have a short offline window 01:15-01:45. Tim will cover during that 30m — Tim, you good to be backup?

tim: Yep, I'll cover 01:15-01:45. Update your handoff notes with that.

jake: I'll update the handoff playbook page with the new mute rules and fallback policy: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/alert-routing — will also add a short checklist for smoke testing.

maria: Quick smoke test before I leave: you can hit the internal test endpoint or ask oncall-bot to fire a synthetic alert. Example: `curl -X POST https://internal-api/_dev/alert-test -d '{"name":"routing-smoke","severity":"warning"}'` or `/alert test routing-smoke` to the bot.

oncall-bot: Test alert routed to #eng-oncall and pager to primary (sophia).

sophia: Received the test, pager notified correctly. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — handing off now. Low risk overall but watch for batch-gpu memory spikes during the prune deploy. I'll leave the playbook updates in the doc and tag the deploy PR.

sophia: Thanks, noted. I'll post any noisy alerts into the thread if we need to revert.

jake: Nice and tidy handoff. I'll also add an entry in the rotation notes that we tried dedup_on: instance_id in the fallback policy (helps reduce duplicate pages)"
